title: 2026 Dental Industry Statistics: A $185B Market at a Crossroads
summary: The U.S. dental market hits $185B in 2026 — but insurance issues, staffing gaps, and rising costs are squeezing practices. Get the key stats and what they mean for your practice.
body_text: The U.S. Dental Industry in 2026: Strong Growth, Real Pressure The U.S. dental industry is, by almost any measure, a growth story. Market revenues are climbing, cosmetic dentistry is booming, and long-term demographic tailwinds remain firmly in place. But behind those headline numbers, a more complicated picture is emerging — one where practice owners are navigating a fiscal squeeze that is testing the resilience of independent dentists and small group practices alike. This article pulls together the most current data available as of mid-2026 to give dental practice owners, office managers, and DSO operators a clear-eyed view of where the industry stands, what's driving the pressure, and where the opportunities lie. Market Size and Growth: The Big Picture Numbers A $185 Billion Industry — and Climbing According to Precedence Research , the U.S. dental services market is estimated at $174.91 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $185.39 billion in 2026 — a meaningful jump in a single year. Looking further out, the market is forecast to hit approximately $281.20 billion by 2035 , expanding at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.86% over the next decade. That's a compelling long-term trajectory. But it's worth pairing that figure with the more granular industry-level data from IBISWorld , which tracks the U.S. dentists industry specifically. IBISWorld projects revenue to reach $196.1 billion in 2026 , with growth of 1.9% in 2026 and a five-year CAGR of just 1.2% . The gap between these two figures reflects different scopes of measurement — Precedence captures the broader dental services ecosystem, while IBISWorld focuses on dentist-operated practices — but both confirm the same directional story: steady, moderate growth. Global Context: A Market Accelerating Faster Overseas The global dental market tells an even more dramatic story. Towards Healthcare reports that the global dental market grew to $49.58 billion in 2026 (up from $44.33 billion in 2025) and is projected to reach $135.73 billion by 2035 , expanding at a CAGR of 11.84% between 2026 and 2035. That's more than double the U.S. growth rate, driven largely by expanding middle-class populations in Asia-Pacific markets and increasing access to dental care in emerging economies. For U.S.-based practices, this global context matters for two reasons: it signals where dental supply chains and technology investment are heading, and it underscores that the fundamentals of dental demand are strong — even if domestic practice economics are under pressure. Cosmetic Dentistry: The Fastest-Growing Segment One of the most striking data points in 2026 is the acceleration of cosmetic dentistry. According to URBN Dental , the global cosmetic dentistry market is expected to be worth $31.31 billion in 2026 — representing 8.55% growth over 2025. Within that segment, clear aligners are projected at $4.77 billion (a 13% jump from 2025) and teeth whitening at $9.37 billion . For practices that have invested in cosmetic services, these numbers represent a genuine revenue opportunity. The challenge, as we'll explore below, is converting that opportunity into accepted treatment plans — a problem that affects far more practices than most owners realize. Dentist Confidence: A Tale of Two Economies Optimistic About Their Own Practice, Worried About the Broader Economy The ADA Health Policy Institute's Q1 2026 State of the U.S. Dental Economy report captures a fascinating split in dentist sentiment. In Q1 2026, 67.5% of dentists reported being 'somewhat' or 'very' confident in their own practice — a reasonably healthy confidence level. But only 32.5% expressed confidence in the overall U.S. economy . This divergence is telling. Dentists, by and large, believe in their own ability to run a good practice. What they're less sure about is whether the macroeconomic environment — inflation, consumer spending, insurance dynamics — will cooperate. That uncertainty is shaping how practices invest, hire, and plan for the year ahead. One in Three Dentists Isn't Busy Enough Perhaps the most sobering statistic in the current landscape: one third of dentists say they are not busy enough heading into 2026, according to data cited by The 10 Minute Dental Marketing Podcast , drawing on ADA HPI Q4 2025 and Henry Schein One 2026 Trends Report data. That figure deserves to sit alongside the market growth numbers. Yes, the industry is growing. But a significant minority of practices are struggling to fill their schedules — which means the growth is not evenly distributed. Larger groups and well-positioned practices are capturing a disproportionate share of patient volume, while smaller independents are feeling the squeeze. For practices in this position, tools like PatientDesk's AI booking system — which provides 24/7 appointment booking and call handling — represent a practical way to capture more of the appointments that are already being sought but going unanswered after hours or during busy periods. The Fiscal Squeeze: Costs Rising Faster Than Revenue The Supply-Demand Imbalance in Practice Economics The core financial challenge facing dental practices in 2026 is straightforward but painful: the expense side of the ledger is rising faster than the revenue side . As the ADA's Dental Sound Bites podcast noted in its Season 7 industry predictions episode: "It's still 90% of practices report it's very or extremely challenging to hire hygienists, and that's been pretty steady. So, the staffing issues are definitely real. And again, overhead costs relate to the issue that look, the supply side, the expense side of dental practice ledger, honestly, like, it's rising. The prices are rising faster than the revenue side prices, which is reimbursement, right? So, we do have this kind of fiscal squeeze." — ADA Health Policy Institute Equipment costs rose 5% last year while reimbursement rates stayed flat, according to data cited by The 10 Minute Dental Marketing Podcast . When you layer in rising labor costs, rent increases, and utility expenses, the margin compression becomes significant — particularly for smaller independent practices that lack the economies of scale available to larger dental groups. IBISWorld's 2026 industry analysis confirms this dynamic explicitly, noting that larger dental groups are better positioned to absorb these pressures through consolidated purchasing, shared administrative infrastructure, and greater leverage in insurance negotiations. Insurance: Now the #1 Challenge For the first time in recent memory, insurance issues have overtaken staffing as the number one challenge reported by dental practices heading into 2026, according to the ADA Dental Sound Bites Season 7, Episode 2 . This finding holds across urban and rural practices and different practice modalities — it's a universal pain point, not a niche concern. The insurance challenge is multifaceted: flat reimbursement rates, increasing claim denials, complex prior authorization requirements, and the administrative burden of managing multiple payer relationships. For many practices, the time and staff resources consumed by insurance administration represent a significant hidden cost. Treatment Acceptance: The Revenue Leak Nobody Talks About Enough Here's a number that should give every practice owner pause: only 47% of recommended treatments are accepted by patients , according to data cited by The 10 Minute Dental Marketing Podcast . That means more than half of the clinical work dentists recommend — work that patients genuinely need — never gets scheduled. Patient affordability is a growing driver of this gap. As JR CPA's 2026 Dental Industry Outlook notes, rising out-of-pocket costs and shifting insurance models have created a more price-sensitive patient base, making flexible payment options a necessity rather than a courtesy for practice owners. This is precisely where technology can make a measurable difference. PatientDesk's AI Patient Sales Coordinator is designed to automate patient follow-up and outbound calls specifically to recover revenue from unaccepted treatment plans — turning that 47% acceptance rate into a target to beat rather than a ceiling to accept. Staffing Shortages: A Persistent Structural Problem The Hygienist Crisis Is Not Letting Up The dental staffing shortage is not a new story, but the 2026 data confirms it remains as acute as ever. According to OpenLoop Health , approximately 95% of dentists find recruiting dental hygienists extremely or very challenging , and 87% report similar difficulties hiring dental assistants . These figures have remained stubbornly high for multiple years running. The practical consequence is significant: labor shortages have caused an estimated 11% reduction in dental practice capacity nationwide . That's not a rounding error — it represents real appointment slots that can't be filled, real revenue that can't be captured, and real patients who aren't getting the care they need. The Capacity Paradox The staffing shortage creates a paradox that many practice owners are living with daily: they have more demand than they can serve, yet they're simultaneously struggling to grow revenue because they can't hire the clinical staff to expand capacity. Meanwhile, administrative overhead — the non-clinical work of running a practice — continues to consume staff time that could otherwise be directed toward patient care. This is the context in which front desk automation becomes not just a convenience but a strategic necessity. PatientDesk's front desk automation features — including real-time insurance verification, payment collection, and practice management system integration — help practices maintain operations without adding headcount, directly addressing the capacity reduction caused by staffing shortages. Why Larger Groups Have the Advantage The staffing challenge is one of the clearest illustrations of why larger dental groups are gaining ground on independent practices. DSOs and multi-location groups can offer more competitive compensation packages, more predictable scheduling, career development pathways, and the kind of workplace infrastructure that attracts and retains clinical talent. Independent practices competing for the same limited pool of hygienists and assistants are often at a structural disadvantage. Patient Demand and Public Health: The Long-Term Drivers Untreated Dental Disease Remains a Massive Unmet Need The demand side of the dental equation is not going away. According to projections based on CDC studies cited by Imagine Your Smile , untreated cavities are expected to affect 1 in 4 U.S. adults by 2026 , with rates significantly higher in rural and underserved communities. This represents both a public health challenge and a long-term demand driver for dental services. The aging population adds another layer to this picture. The U.S. senior population is projected to reach 92 million by 2060 , and older adults have complex, ongoing dental needs — from restorative work to periodontal care to implants. Practices that position themselves to serve this demographic effectively are investing in a durable growth opportunity. Geographic and Demographic Disparities The distribution of dental need — and dental access — is highly uneven. Rural and underserved communities face both higher rates of untreated disease and fewer available providers. For practices in these markets, the demand is there; the challenge is operational capacity and patient affordability. For practices in competitive urban markets, the challenge is differentiation and patient retention in an increasingly crowded landscape. Technology Adoption: From Early Adopter to Table Stakes AI and Digital Workflows Are Going Mainstream One of the most significant shifts in 2026 is the normalization of AI-powered tools in dental practice. According to Pearl AI's analysis of major challenges facing dentists , AI-driven radiographic interpretation, CBCT tools, and integrated digital workflows are moving from early adoption into everyday dental practice. Practice management automation — including AI-powered insurance verification, billing, patient communication, and scheduling — is deepening following widespread adoption throughout 2025. This is no longer a conversation about whether to adopt technology. It's a conversation about which tools to prioritize and how to integrate them effectively into existing workflows. The ROI Case for Automation The business case for practice automation in 2026 is clearer than it's ever been. When staffing costs are rising, reimbursement rates are flat, and administrative burden is increasing, automation that reduces manual work — without reducing care quality — directly improves practice economics. The practices that are navigating the fiscal squeeze most successfully are, by and large, the ones that have invested in systems that let their human staff focus on high-value clinical and patient-facing work. What This Means for Independent Practices For independent practices, the technology adoption imperative is both an opportunity and a challenge. The opportunity: automation tools that were once only accessible to large groups are now available at price points that work for single-location practices. The challenge: evaluating, implementing, and integrating new tools takes time and expertise that busy practice owners often don't have in abundance. The practices that will thrive in the second half of this decade are those that treat technology adoption not as a one-time project but as an ongoing operational discipline — continuously evaluating what's working, what's not, and where the next efficiency gain is available. Key Takeaways for Practice Owners and DSO Operators The 2026 dental industry data tells a story of genuine opportunity constrained by real operational headwinds. Here's what the numbers add up to for practice leaders: The market is growing , but growth is not evenly distributed. Practices that aren't actively working to capture their share of demand will find themselves on the wrong side of the average. Insurance is now the top challenge — and it's not going away. Practices need both better administrative systems and a clear strategy for managing payer relationships. Staffing shortages are structural , not cyclical. Waiting for the labor market to improve is not a strategy. Automation and workflow redesign are. Treatment acceptance at 47% is a revenue crisis hiding in plain sight. Every practice should know its own acceptance rate and have a systematic approach to improving it. Technology adoption is accelerating — and the gap between early adopters and laggards is widening. The time to invest in AI-powered practice management tools is now, not after the competition has already done it. Patient affordability is a growing barrier. Flexible payment options, transparent pricing, and proactive financial conversations are becoming competitive differentiators. The dental industry's long-term fundamentals remain strong. The practices that will capture the most value from that growth are the ones that address their operational challenges with the same rigor they bring to clinical care. Want to see how AI-powered front desk automation can help your practice navigate the 2026 landscape? Explore PatientDesk's full feature set or learn more about the AI Patient Sales Coordinator built specifically for dental practices.

title: Aligned, Accurate, and Agile: How Slackbot Powers the Salesforce Legal Team
summary: It’s a common assumption in the business world: Legal, compliance, and risk departments are the last to change their ways. Historically seen as
body_text: It’s a common assumption in the business world: Legal, compliance, and risk departments are the last to change their ways. Historically seen as risk-averse, slow to adopt new technology and protective of established processes, these functions are labeled as often lagging when it comes to enterprise transformation journeys. At Salesforce, we decided to test that assumption and turn it on its head. And in testing it, we may have built something more useful than expected: a replicable playbook for how any organization, in any industry, can responsibly embrace AI and agentic transformation at scale. Salesforce Legal and Corporate Affairs (LCA) is a global team that manages hundreds of thousands of requests per year, and this transformation has fundamentally changed (and continues to change) how we operate, govern, and partner with our colleagues across the company. As Customer Zero for our own technology, LCA is building an AI-native, trust-first, agentic legal function that holds the promise of defining the best of human-AI collaboration. Humans and agents work together to orchestrate agentic workflows. Agents handle routine questions, freeing our attorneys and other legal professionals to focus on what only humans can do: building trust, leading with integrity, and solving high-stakes, complex problems. Team members develop their careers by building agentic fluency, AI skills, and cutting-edge prowess. Beyond productivity, one deeper value is commercial velocity. When legal response time accelerates, when sellers are empowered through effective self-serve delivery models, and when teams are augmented with agentic capabilities, we remove friction, simplify processes, and close deals faster. At scale, this compounds, serving as a true force multiplier for our customers, partners, and business. Here’s part of the playbook we’re building in real time. Slackbot powers our Salesforce legal team To start, we embraced our role as Customer Zero for Slackbot . Slackbot automates routine workflows to give our teams time back to focus on building trust, calibrating risk against opportunity, and navigating high-stakes complexity. The integrated AI companion solves a critical friction point: the need for high-precision internal research, trusted information finding, and document and thread summarization without disruptive context switching. Because Slackbot leverages curated source-of-truth internal knowledge articles and legal resource libraries built by trusted teams, it delivers accurate, consistent guidance the moment our people need it. It’s a real-time intelligence layer that keeps our global team aligned, accurate, and agile. Real-world legal use cases Here’s how Slackbot helps our global legal team move quickly, with trust at the forefront: 1 . We don’t have to search for our data now. We can just talk to it. In the past, checking the status of a main service agreement (MSA) or finding a specific business associate agreement (BAA) contract meant switching between multiple Salesforce instances and databases. By design, Slack and Slackbot work seamlessly alongside core CRM systems and records, including Salesforce, to streamline workflows. Now, my team asks questions in plain English directly in Slackbot, like: “What’s the status of the MSA negotiation with [Company X]?” “Give me a summary of the top three themes in our data privacy requests this year.” Slackbot pulls the answer from our “source of truth” and provides a direct link to the record. No context-switching, no hunting for tabs. 2 . We have streamlined our verification processes. The legal team has built a product legal front door in Slack, a self-serve Slackbot-powered intake experience that helps Technology and Products colleagues get to the right legal resource quickly. Depending on the query, Slackbot can route users to existing legal channels, prompt them to submit a customer case, determine whether a Product Legal Review (PLR) is needed for a new feature or product, or walk them through an intake process for new product partnerships. This is anchored in trusted, structured legal knowledge articles and reliable data, allowing teams to move quickly with confidence. Looking ahead, the team plans to expand self-service capabilities to cover topics like end-of-life processes and nondisclosure agreements (NDAs). 3 . We use Slackbot as our digital assistant. Beyond the specialized legal queries, Slackbot has become a daily productivity companion. We use it to handle the administrative tax of our profession, the fabric of every lawyer’s day, so our human teams can focus on high-value strategy and counsel: Meeting prep and summarization: We can turn an hour-long sync into a bulleted list of action items. Complex document synthesis: We work through 50-page briefs to pull out specific clauses or summarize complex concepts in seconds. Asset creation: We generate initial drafts for documents and presentations, allowing our lawyers to start at 80% completion rather than a blank page. 4. We stress-test legal arguments. This is where it gets interesting for practitioners. Our corporate counsel now uses Slackbot to stress-test arguments before they are finalized. By asking the AI to identify logical fallacies or anticipate potential counterarguments, we aren’t replacing the lawyer’s judgment; we’re sharpening it. It’s about entering a negotiation with a higher level of confidence and getting a better understanding of what our customers may need. Our corporate counsel now uses Slackbot to stress-test arguments before they are finalized A new role for a new era: The agent manager As the legal team integrated AI agents, such as Slackbot, into their daily workflows, it became clear we needed a dedicated role at the intersection of legal expertise and agentic risk. Not a blocker, but an enabler with guardrails. Someone who could proactively mitigate legal and reputational risk without becoming a bottleneck for implementation. So we created a new human role: the agent manager. Our goal was to build a repeatable engine for “yes, here’s how to do it safely,” rather than “no by default.” Over 18 months of manual testing and risk-spotting, our agent manager built and operationalized: A Risk & Impact Scoring System, developed with LCA subject matter experts, to prioritize the testing of high-risk queries and high-impact processes SME “tiger teams,” user acceptance testing frameworks that validate agent accuracy before launch Standardized guardrails and disclaimers with cross-functional teams Automated regression testing to monitor agent performance as models improve, content is updated, and scope increases A checkpoint in the AI Council Review Process that triggers the testing framework whenever a use case is grounded in legal content We’ve made our agent manager role a permanent and core fixture of our team, and every agent deployment they have supported has successfully launched. Having a human sit at the intersection of the legal profession and agentic technology makes agentic deployments successful, with higher trust and adoption within the legal team. The broader lesson: A playbook for the Agentic Enterprise Legal departments are a fascinating test case for AI transformation precisely because of their historical resistance to change. The professional culture values deliberation, precedent, and risk avoidance. The work involves privileged information, reputational exposure, and significant stakes. The talent pool is, by training, skeptical. If AI and agentic transformation can take root and thrive in that environment — and deliver the kind of measurable results, external recognition, and cultural shift we’re seeing — it provides a proof point and a playbook for the entire enterprise. What we are building is also a vital signal to our customers. Our broader ecosystem can look at what we’ve built in LCA and see not just a proof of concept but a model. When organizations navigate their own AI journeys, grappling with data governance, legal exposure, and responsible use, they need to know we hold ourselves to the highest standards. Every guardrail, risk framework, and testing checkpoint we built reflects how AI should be deployed in any high-stakes environment: with intentionality, human accountability, and trust built in from the start. We aren’t asking our customers to go anywhere we haven’t gone ourselves. We are not just adopting trusted AI. We are proving how human and AI collaboration can transform the legal profession — and then sharing what we learn. That is what it means to be Customer Zero.

title: QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release now available
summary: We’re excited to announce the availability of the latest release of QIAGEN Clinical Insight (QCI) Interpret, QCI Interpret One and QCI Interpret Translational. The QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release delivers […] The post QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release now available appeared first on Bioinformatics Software | QIAGEN Digital Insights .
body_text: We’re excited to announce the availability of the latest release of QIAGEN Clinical Insight (QCI) Interpret, QCI Interpret One and QCI Interpret Translational. The QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release delivers new capabilities designed to further streamline variant interpretation and reporting. QCI Interpret is leading clinical interpretation platform by case volume, used to analyze and interpret more than 5.5 million NGS tests cases worldwide. Now, with the latest release, the platform now provides enhanced end-to-end variant interpretation and reporting with improved classification workflows, integrated sample QC and multilingual reporting capabilities. What's new in the QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release? Built-in comment translation for multilingual reporting Report comments can now be translated into the preferred language directly within QCI Interpret, eliminating the need for external translation tools. Translation of overall, additional and variant-specific comments are supported. Translated comments can be viewed, edited, saved, compared with the original English and included in both the final report and XML export (not available in QCI Interpret Translational). → Request a sample translated QCI Interpret report here . Streamlined Quality Control (QC) assessment QCI Interpret now supports ingestion of secondary-analysis quality metrics through a structured JSON QC file, making sample quality data available alongside variant interpretation in a single workflow. Standardized QC status tags and a dedicated Sample QC view provide immediate clarity on data quality, and QC metrics can be included in the final PDF report through template-driven reporting (not available in QCI Interpret Translational). New Batch Create feature for multiple tests Now, up to 200 tests can be created in a single step by uploading a CSV sample sheet via the new Batch Create button on the Test List and Sample List pages. A validation page reviews the submission before test creation proceeds, ensuring errors are identified and resolved upfront (not available in QCI Interpret Translational). New Previous Occurrences column in the Variant List page The new Previous Occurrences column on the Variant List page displays how many times each variant was previously seen. The count is captured as a snapshot at test creation, reflects all prior tests accessible to the test creator and is hyperlinked to the corresponding variant-specific page in the Variant Directory. The column is enabled by default and can be toggled off from Settings (not available in QCI Interpret Translational). NGS and orthogonal data consolidation in a single report JSON files and PDF documents can now be uploaded alongside a test via the UI or API. Reports customized through QIAGEN Services can be configured to extract and display data from uploaded JSON files and/or append PDF documents to the end of the final report, enabling fully integrated reporting of NGS alongside orthogonal data results (not available in QCI Interpret Translational). Expanded Bulk Assessment tool The Bulk Assessment tool now provides access to the full range of pathogenicity, actionability and reportability options when assessing multiple variants at once, consistent with what is available for single-variant assessments. A select-all checkbox makes it faster to act on all variants in the current view, and a confirmation page previews all proposed changes before they are applied (not available in QCI Interpret Translational). Structural duplications now displayed as a distinct alteration type Previously, variants encoded as structural duplications were treated and displayed as amplifications. Now, QCI Interpret recognizes structural duplications as a distinct alteration type, displaying them accurately across the platform. Content matching for structural duplications includes "mutation positive" and related specificities in addition to amplification content, supporting more precise variant review in both somatic and hereditary workflows. Updated ACMG/AMP classification logic and refined HGVS nomenclature The QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release introduces updated ACMG/AMP classification logic and refined HGVS nomenclature. Improvements to criteria logic, default strengths and classification rules may result in changes to computed classifications or actionability designations for a subset of variants. These changes do not impact prior assessments saved by the user. Explore the full list of new features available in the QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release. See what's new The post QCI Interpret Summer 2026 Release now available appeared first on Bioinformatics Software | QIAGEN Digital Insights .

title: Portable WiFi for Motorhome Holidays and Road Trips in 2026
summary: Searching for dependable internet on your motorhome adventures? Discover how mobile hotspots work, compare your connection choices, and stay online across Europe in 2026.
body_text: For today's travellers, staying online is no longer a nice-to-have – it's a necessity. Whether you're handling remote work from a campsite in the Lake District, streaming a film after a long day behind the wheel, or simply checking in with loved ones back home, dependable internet has become an indispensable part of the modern motorhome experience. That said, connectivity on the road remains notoriously unpredictable. Campsite WiFi is often overloaded, mobile coverage varies drastically from one region to another, and public networks frequently come with privacy risks. This is precisely why more and more holidaymakers are turning to portable WiFi for motorhome travel as a flexible and trustworthy solution to stay connected. Today's portable hotspots go far beyond basic internet sharing. Many advanced models can automatically roam between available carrier networks, support numerous devices at the same time, and offer all-day battery life – making them practical companions for everything from weekend getaways to full-time van-life adventures. Why Dependable Motorhome Internet Matters More Than Ever The way we travel has undergone a significant shift in recent years. Motorhome holidays have become increasingly connected. Whether you're touring the Scottish Highlands, crossing the Alps, or spending several weeks meandering through European countryside, reliable internet can make your journey smoother and more enjoyable. These days, internet access is about much more than just checking emails. Motorhome travellers often depend on connectivity for: GPS navigation and live traffic information Booking campsites, attractions, and ferry crossings Streaming films, music, and podcasts during downtime Staying in touch with family and friends across time zones Uploading holiday photos and sharing experiences on social media Checking weather forecasts and receiving travel alerts While cities and popular tourist hubs usually offer public Wi-Fi, many motorhome routes traverse rural areas where connectivity can be patchy at best. A stable internet connection helps travellers stay informed, entertained, and connected throughout their journey – no matter which direction the road takes them. Common Connectivity Challenges for Motorhome Travellers Before choosing a hotspot, it's worth understanding the typical hurdles travellers face while on the move. Campsite Wi-Fi Is Often Unreliable Many campsites advertise complimentary Wi-Fi, but the reality rarely matches the promise. During peak hours – evenings and weekends – dozens or even hundreds of guests may be sharing the same network. As more people stream content, browse social media, and connect multiple gadgets, speeds can plummet to a crawl. For travellers who rely on internet access for work or important communications, campsite Wi-Fi is best treated as a fallback option rather than a primary connection. Mobile Coverage Can Vary Dramatically Between Destinations One day you might be parked near a bustling city with excellent 4G or 5G coverage. The next, you could be exploring a remote national park in the Pyrenees where signal strength is barely detectable. This inconsistency is a key reason why many travellers prefer portable WiFi devices that can tap into multiple carrier networks, rather than being locked into a single provider. The Breakthrough Solutions: CloudSIM and Smart Cellular Technology To overcome the limitations of congested campsite infrastructure and single-carrier dead zones, modern portable WiFi devices have evolved significantly. How CloudSIM Technology Eliminates Dead Zones Traditional mobile hotspots rely on a physical SIM card tied to one specific carrier (such as Vodafone, EE, or O2 in the UK). CloudSIM technology completely reimagines this approach. Instead of a physical card, it stores carrier profiles digitally in the cloud. When a motorhome moves into a new region, a CloudSIM-enabled device automatically scans the area, identifies which local network offers the strongest signal, and switches to that carrier in real time. For travellers crossing borders within Europe, this eliminates the need to buy multiple local SIM cards or endure frustrating dropped connections. Do You Really Need a 5G Hotspot? As you explore portable WiFi options, you'll frequently encounter the 5G versus 4G LTE debate. While 5G delivers impressive speeds in urban centres, its high-frequency signals struggle to penetrate rural landscapes and dense woodlands. For the majority of motorhome routes, a robust 4G LTE connection provides more than enough performance for HD streaming, video calls, navigation, and everyday browsing. The best device isn't the one with the highest theoretical speed in a city – it's the one that delivers consistent, reliable coverage in the countryside. Portable WiFi vs. Satellite Internet: Which Is Right for You? Beyond cellular hotspots, satellite internet has also gained attention among travellers. While satellite systems are invaluable for deep wilderness expeditions, they are not a one-size-fits-all solution. When comparing the two, portable cellular WiFi devices typically offer: Significantly lower upfront costs: No expensive satellite dish hardware to purchase. True portability: Compact, lightweight designs that fit easily into a pocket or glovebox. Instant setup: No need to align dishes or find a clear view of the sky. Connectivity while moving: Works seamlessly while the vehicle is in motion. While satellite internet is ideal for off-grid adventurers who spend weeks in remote areas completely untouched by mobile networks, portable WiFi remains the most practical, cost-effective, and convenient choice for standard road trips and typical motorhome holidays across Europe. Features to Look for in a Portable WiFi Device If you decide that a portable WiFi hotspot suits your travel style, prioritise the following features during your search: Extended Battery Life Battery performance can make a real difference during travel days and off-grid camping. A hotspot that lasts throughout a full day of driving helps reduce charging interruptions and makes it easier to stay connected away from power sources. Some travel-focused devices, such as the GlocalMe MeowGo G40 Pro , are engineered with portability and extended battery life in mind. With up to 15 hours of operation on a single charge, they can support travellers through long driving days and extended periods away from electrical hookups. Flexible Network Access Coverage can change rapidly as you move between cities, motorways, campsites, and rural destinations. Devices that can intelligently access available carrier networks often deliver a more consistent motorhome internet experience than solutions tied to a single provider. Multi-Device Capacity Most travellers carry more than one connected device. Smartphones, tablets, laptops, and streaming gadgets frequently share the same connection. Whether you're using portable WiFi for motorhome travel or setting up portable WiFi for car trips with family and friends, choosing a device that supports multiple simultaneous connections can greatly improve convenience for everyone on board. Travel-Friendly Design Space is always at a premium when travelling. Compact devices are easier to store, simpler to carry, and more convenient to position for optimal signal reception. Some travellers also appreciate devices that combine multiple functions into a single unit. For example, the UniCord Pro 4G global WiFi hotspot integrates portable WiFi functionality with charging capabilities, helping to reduce the number of accessories needed during a trip. Practical Tips for Improving Motorhome Internet Performance Once you have your portable WiFi device, put these field-tested strategies to work to maximise its performance: Position Strategically: Signal quality is heavily influenced by physical obstructions. Always place your hotspot near a window or on an elevated shelf inside the motorhome to minimise interference from the vehicle's aluminium or fibreglass body panels. Monitor Data Consumption: Video streaming is the quickest way to eat through your data allowance. Lowering your streaming settings from 4K to standard HD, or downloading offline maps and content ahead of time, can significantly extend your data plan. Maintain a Multi-Network Backup: Experienced travellers always keep a secondary connection option – such as a low-cost local SIM or using campsite Wi-Fi for non-essential tasks – to ensure they're never completely cut off in an emergency. Update Software Before You Leave: Download all system and application updates while connected to your home broadband. Doing this before departure prevents background updates from consuming precious mobile data on the road. Stay Connected Wherever Your Motorhome Journey Takes You Reliable internet has become a cornerstone of modern travel. Whether you're plotting a weekend escape or managing a full-time remote career from the open road, the right connectivity solution reduces stress and expands your freedom. By aligning your portable WiFi choices with your specific destinations and device needs, you can spend far less time hunting for a signal and far more time savouring the journey ahead. FAQ Is portable WiFi worth it for motorhome travel? For travellers who regularly work online, stream content, or visit multiple destinations, portable WiFi typically offers a more reliable and secure connection than relying solely on campsite Wi-Fi. Can I use portable WiFi while driving? Yes. Most portable hotspots continue to function while the vehicle is moving, allowing passengers to stay connected during road trips. Does portable WiFi work in remote camping areas? Performance depends on local mobile coverage. Devices that support multiple carrier networks may improve connectivity options, although extremely remote locations can still have limited service. Is portable WiFi for car travel different from portable WiFi for motorhome travel? In most cases, the same hotspot can be used for both. The main differences are how many devices need to connect and how frequently the internet connection is used during travel.

title: Como melhorar no xadrez: dicas para todos os níveis
summary: Desenvolva as suas táticas no jogo e faça o Óscar ter medo do seu xeque-mate.
body_text: 23 jul 2026 Katherine Wise Como melhorar no xadrez: dicas para todos os níveis Desenvolva as suas táticas no jogo e faça o Óscar ter medo do seu xeque-mate. 23 jul 2026 Katherine Wise Se você sonha em derrotar o Óscar no curso de xadrez do Duolingo , provavelmente já está pensando bastante em como melhorar as suas táticas! Não importa o seu nível no xadrez: jogar uma partida por dia (ou mais!) vai colocar você no rumo certo para evoluir 📈 Confira abaixo algumas dicas para jogar melhor. Dicas para iniciantes no xadrez Se você é estreante no xadrez, daqui para a frente é só progresso! Aqui estão algumas formas de evoluir no jogo. 📚 Aprenda xeques-mates básicos Um ótimo primeiro passo é aprender xeques-mates básicos, especialmente: dar xeque-mate com uma dama sozinha dar xeque-mate com uma torre dar xeque-mate com duas torres (muitas vezes chamado de “mate escadinha”) Mesmo que você tenha uma dama a mais, isso não vai adiantar se não souber usar essa vantagem para dar xeque-mate no adversário! Com a prática, você logo conseguirá dar xeque-mate com eficiência mesmo sob pressão, sem correr o risco de esquecer como finaliza a partida 😅 ⏳ Jogue partidas mais lentas Partidas mais lentas (e mais longas) permitem que você pense em cada lance em vez de sair jogando como se fosse um supercomputador . Desafie-se a jogar pelo menos uma partida lenta por semana, com pelo menos 20 a 60 minutos para cada pessoa. Partidas rápidas, como blitz ou bullet , são divertidas, mas dependem muito da intuição e, por isso, não são ideais para iniciantes. Já as partidas mais lentas dão a você a chance de praticar cálculo, visualização e pensamento estratégico. 🧠 Escolha adversários fortes Jogar contra adversários mais avançados, e não mais iniciantes, vai ajudar você a fortalecer as suas estratégias! É da natureza humana gostar de vencer, mas você não vai perceber os seus próprios erros — e, consequentemente, melhorar — jogando contra pessoas de nível muito inferior ao seu. Os erros fazem parte do aprendizado. Você nunca vai esquecer aquela vez em que perdeu uma partida que já estava praticamente ganha! ♻️ Treine táticas de xadrez No xadrez, tática se refere a sequências de lances curtas e forçadas que dão uma vantagem imediata. Garfos, cravadas, espetos e ataques descobertos são alguns exemplos de táticas. Praticar diferentes tipos de tática ajuda a desenvolver um reconhecimento de padrões que é essencial, especialmente para jogadores que estão começando agora. Em partidas de iniciantes, as capivaradas acontecem o tempo todo, então você terá muitas chances de encontrar uma tática vencedora e virar uma partida. (Sim, mesmo que você tenha conseguido perder sua dama no quinto lance!) Dicas para jogadores de xadrez intermediários Se você já domina o básico e quer partir para um novo desafio, aqui vão algumas ideias: 🤖 Analise as suas partidas com uma engine de xadrez Use o computador para turbinar as suas estratégias! Preste atenção às suas maiores capivaradas, assim como às maiores mudanças na avaliação da engine (motor), ou seja, os momentos em que um dos jogadores passou de vencedor a perdedor, ou vice-versa. Concentre-se em alguns dos seus maiores erros de cada partida e tente entender qual foi o problema. Você deixou uma peça pendurada porque a colocou direto na linha de ataque do adversário? Ou esqueceu que uma peça estava defendendo outra e acabou tirando a defensora do posto sem perceber?! 🫣 Para ajudar a identificar e entender os seus erros, veja os lances sugeridos pela engine e compare com os lances que você fez. 🤓 Estude aberturas Familiarize-se com as aberturas mais comuns e tente encontrar aquelas que combinam com você e o seu estilo de jogo. Escolha pelo menos uma abertura para as peças brancas e uma para as peças pretas; depois, estude as variantes mais usadas de cada uma. À medida que evoluir, aprenda mais aberturas para cada cor, assim você conseguirá responder aos lances mais comuns. Por exemplo: jogando de pretas, aprenda uma abertura para responder a 1. e4 das brancas e outra para responder a 1. d4. Dessa forma, você saberá como reagir a qualquer movimento do seu adversário! Dicas para jogadores de xadrez avançados Mesmo jogadores avançados ainda podem continuar evoluindo! 🔍 Foque nos finais de jogo Quanto mais avançado for o seu nível, maior a chance de a partida ser decidida no final, depois de uma longa batalha de mais de 50 lances. Já ficaram para trás os dias de pendurar uma peça nos primeiros 10 lances. (Bom, na maior parte do tempo, pelo menos…) Comece pelos finais de rei e peão, depois passe para os finais de torre e deixe os finais mais complicados para mais tarde. Conceitos introdutórios como oposição e triangulação já serão extremamente úteis em muitos finais — não é preciso mergulhar imediatamente nas complexidades dos finais de bispo e cavalo! Seu próximo lance é praticar! A melhor forma de evoluir no xadrez é encontrar o que te motiva e faz você se apaixonar por esse jogo. Quanto mais você jogar, mais vai progredir — e mais vai se divertir também! TAGS Xadrez (PT) Aprendizagem (PT) Dicas e truques (PT) Motivação (PT) COMPARTILHAR

title: UiPath Alternatives for Insurance Brokers: When Each One Fits
summary: A buyer guide for brokerages comparing legacy RPA, carrier APIs, AI agents, and BPO for AMS-to-carrier work.
body_text: [Vendor comparison] Insurance brokerages do not need a generic automation category. They need a way to move data between AMS records, carrier portals, quote forms, appetite guides, and follow-up queues without turning every carrier into an integration project. Legacy RPA fits controlled broker workflows A platform like UiPath can fit when the brokerage controls the application surface and wants to automate a stable sequence, such as an internal report or a predictable admin task. The challenge starts when the workflow leaves the brokerage stack and enters carrier websites, wholesaler portals, PDF forms, and email attachments. Carrier APIs do not cover enough of the work APIs are valuable where they exist, but broker operations often depend on long-tail carrier portals that do not expose the exact action the team needs. BPO can absorb the work, but it adds queue time, handoff risk, and management overhead. UI agents sit between those options by operating the same portals directly while keeping the workflow auditable. The right alternative depends on the bottleneck If the bottleneck is a stable internal task, use RPA. If the bottleneck is carrier portal submission, quote intake, appetite checks, or document transfer, prioritize an agent that can work through the UI. For brokerages, the decision should be made workflow by workflow, not vendor by vendor. Brokerage rule Choose the tool based on where the work breaks: internal system, carrier portal, document queue, or human judgment.

title: Tipi di nylon: un confronto
summary: Confronto tra polipropilene e polietilene: le proprietà che rendono entrambi una scelta popolare per i clienti.
body_text: Tutti abbiamo sentito parlare del nylon e la maggior parte di noi lo utilizza ogni giorno. Sintetizzato per la prima volta nel 1935 dal chimico Wallace Carothers di DuPont, questo noto polimero fu inizialmente impiegato per sostituire la seta nelle calze da donna. Ma la Seconda guerra mondiale ne ampliò notevolmente l’impiego e, in breve tempo, il nuovo materiale trovò applicazione in tutto: dai paracadute agli pneumatici per camion, dalle tende ai serbatoi di carburant e. Oggi è una delle fibre sintetiche più diffuse e utilizzate. Che cos'è il nylon? Il nylon è una famiglia di poliammidi (PA), un gruppo di polimeri sintetici e, in alcuni casi, di origine naturale, basati su legami ammide (un gruppo carbonilico legato a un atomo di azoto) che offrono elevata resistenza e durabilità. Altri esempi includono Kevlar, Nomex, Pebax e materiali ad alte prestazioni simili. Come il nylon, anche questi materiali presentano caratteristiche vantaggiose: il Kevlar, ad esempio, è noto per la sua tenacità, che ne ha favorito l’impiego nei giubbotti antiproiettile, mentre il Nomex è spesso utilizzato nell’abbigliamento protettivo contro il fuoco . Naturalmente, non produciamo capi di abbigliamento, ma realizziamo un’ampia varietà di componenti unici e di alta qualità utilizzando oltre due dozzine di gradi di nylon. In questo articolo analizziamo alcune delle proprietà e delle applicazioni di questi diversi materiali e accenniamo alle tecnologie di produzione impiegate per lavorarli. Nylon 6 (PA 6): resistente, ma da tenere lontano dall’acqua Passeggiando nelle nostre officine meccaniche, potresti vedere pezzi lavorati tramite fresatura CNC in PA 6, un tipo di nylon sintetizzato a partire dal composto organico caprolattame. Le catene polimeriche del nylon 6 sono costituite da anelli ripetuti di sei atomi di carbonio ciascuno, da cui deriva il nome. Come altri nylon, il PA 6 è noto per l’elevata resistenza a trazione, la tenacità e l’elasticità. Tuttavia, presenta una marcata capacità di assorbire umidità, che può influire negativamente sulla stabilità dimensionale e sulle proprietà meccaniche. Il nylon 6 fonde intorno a 428°F (220°C). È resistente a numerosi agenti chimici, oli e solventi; è autolubrificante e offre una buona resistenza all’abrasione. Con un peso pari a circa un ottavo di quello del bronzo, il nylon 6 è adatto ad applicazioni quali ingranaggi e boccole, parti automobilistiche come collettori di aspirazione e coperture del motore e, grazie alle sue proprietà elettriche, è spesso utilizzato per isolatori e connettori . Offriamo due gradi di nylon 6 colato, PA 6 nero e PA 6 blu; quest’ultimo è stabilizzato termicamente e consente un aumento del 10% della temperatura di esercizio. Nylon 6/6: più tenace e più resistente all’usura Che differenza possono fare pochi atomi di carbonio! Il nylon 6/6 (noto anche come Nylon 66 o PA 6/6) è sintetizzato a partire da due monomeri (acido adipico ed esametilendiammina), ognuno dei quali contribuisce con catene di sei atomi di carbonio, da cui deriva il suffisso 6/6. Queste unità ripetute aumentano la resistenza a trazione, la tenacità e la durabilità del materiale rispetto al nylon 6, riducendone al contempo la tendenza ad assorbire umidità e innalzandone il punto di fusione a circa 500°F (260°C). Questo rende il nylon 6/6 una sorta di “fratello maggiore” del nylon 6: più tenace, più robusto (circa il 20%) e più resistente all’usura, pur essendo impiegato in molte delle stesse applicazioni. Nella nostra officina meccanica sono disponibili due gradi: nylon 6/6 naturale e nylon 6/6 caricato con fibra di vetro (ne parleremo più avanti), mentre il servizio di stampaggio a iniezione offre numerose varianti di PA 66, per lo più con l’aggiunta di materiali di carica. Ne parleremo a breve. Nylon 6/12 (PA 6/12): resistenza all’umidità per lo stampaggio Nel reparto di stampaggio a iniezione delle materie plastiche si trova anche il nylon 6/12, caratterizzato da unità alternate dei monomeri esametilendiammina (con 6 atomi di carbonio) e acido dodecanedioico (12 atomi di carbonio). È un po’ meno resistente del PA 6 o del PA 66 e ha una temperatura di fusione intermedia tra i due, ma è meno soggetto all’assorbimento di umidità rispetto a entrambi. Le setole del tuo spazzolino potrebbero essere in PA 6/12, così come le linee carburante della tua auto, la guaina dei cavi elettrici, le cerniere della tua tenda da campeggio e molte altre applicazioni in cui serve un grado di nylon più stabile e resistente all’umidità. Per lo stampaggio a iniezione offriamo una versione di poliammide 6/12 con il 33% di carica di fibra di vetro (Zytel 77G33L NC010), che DuPont definisce un “polimero performante”, con additivi per migliorare la lubrificazione e la stampabilità. Nylon 11 (PA 11): stampare una plastica sostenibile Passiamo ora alla stampa 3D. Il PA 11 è sintetizzato a partire dall’acido 11-aminoundecanoico, un monomero derivato dall’olio di ricino. Questo lo rende uno dei nylon più “verdi”, anche se tutti presentano criticità in termini di riciclo. Come avrai ormai intuito, ogni unità ripetuta delle catene polimeriche del nylon 11 contiene 11 atomi di carbonio. Nei nostri sistemi di stampa 3D SLS (sinterizzazione laser selettiva) utilizziamo polvere di PA 11 nero. Il materiale offre un ottimo equilibrio tra resistenza e flessibilità, oltre a un’eccellente resistenza agli urti, soprattutto a basse temperature. Inoltre assorbe meno umidità rispetto al nylon 6 o 6/6, garantendo una migliore stabilità dimensionale in condizioni umide, ma ha un punto di fusione più basso, pari a 410°F (210°C). Unendo queste qualità a un’elevata resistenza ai raggi UV, il PA 11 risulta una scelta di primo piano per molte applicazioni outdoor, ad esempio scarponi da sci e altri articoli sportivi, oppure componenti con incastri a scatto e cerniere flessibili. Nylon 12 (PA 12): ottime prestazioni con una diversa struttura molecolare Il PA 12 è un altro materiale di riferimento, utilizzato sia nella stampa 3D SLS sia nei processi Multi Jet Fusion. È una poliammide alifatica lineare, il che significa che la sua struttura è composta da catene aperte di atomi di carbonio (12, in questo caso) anziché da anelli. Presenta un’eccellente resistenza chimica, in particolare verso diversi agenti chimici, sali e oli, ma ha un punto di fusione più basso, intorno a 356°F (180°C). Inoltre, come il PA 11, assorbe meno umidità rispetto ad altre poliammidi, risultando stabile dimensionalmente in un’ampia gamma di condizioni ambientali. Sono disponibili gradi neri e bianchi, oltre a versioni caricate con fibra di vetro e con cariche minerali, che migliorano le proprietà meccaniche e termiche del PA 12. Contenitori e dispositivi sono spesso realizzati in PA 12 (pieni o cavi), così come alcuni cateteri e altri componenti medicali (il PA 12 è tra i nylon più biocompatibili), sistemi di alimentazione automobilistica, imballaggi per cosmetici, connettori elettrici e molto altro. Le cariche: una panoramica Come indicato in precedenza, offriamo circa due dozzine di gradi di nylon destinati al solo stampaggio a iniezione. Con poche eccezioni, la maggior parte di questi si basa sul nylon 66 con diversi tipi di cariche. I nylon rinforzati con fibra di vetro sono i più comuni: come suggerisce il nome, sono rinforzati con fibra di vetro per migliorarne la resistenza meccanica, la rigidità e la stabilità dimensionale . La percentuale varia dal 13% (Hylon Select N1013HL) al 33% ( Vydyne R533H e Zytel 70G33 sono due esempi). Sono disponibili anche nylon rinforzati con cariche minerali, come Minlon 10B40, e nylon che contengono modificanti d’urto ( Zytel ST-80) o stabilizzanti UV (RTP 200 200 UV). Come già osservato, questi e diversi altri nylon “speciali” garantiscono prestazioni superiori nelle applicazioni più impegnative, sebbene a un prezzo premium. Infine, tieni presente che, sebbene le cariche di fibra di vetro e le cariche minerali apportino benefici significativi nello stampaggio a iniezione, sono anche più abrasive rispetto alle versioni non caricate e tendono a consumare più rapidamente cavità e anime dello stampo. Come sempre, puoi rivolgerti al tuo referente Protolabs per ricevere consigli sulla scelta del polimero, sulla progettazione dello stampo e su altri aspetti produttivi già nelle prime fasi di sviluppo del progetto, così da evitare problemi in seguito. Richiedi un preventivo È il momento di dare forma al tuo progetto con il nylon più adatto. Carica il tuo pezzo per ottenere subito prezzi e tempi di consegna per PA 6, PA 6/6, PA 11, PA 12 e per i gradi rinforzati con fibra di vetro o con cariche minerali.
